title: Format of Government's After-action Review on COVID-19 and Plans to Share Review Findings or Recommendations
what_it_is: Format of Government's After-action Review on COVID-19 and Plans to Share Review Findings or Recommendations

sections.label: After-action review of pandemic response
sections.summary: The Government has started an after-action review of the outbreak's first phase, overseen by former Head of Civil Service Peter Ho, with findings to be shared publicly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: For now, the pandemic is still not over, but the situation has improved.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Therefore, the Government has started work on the AAR, focusing on the first phase of our experience, in other words, what happened from the start of the outbreak till August 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The AAR is intended as a broad ranging exercise to thoroughly analyse our experiences and review the lessons learnt, so that we can be better prepared for the next pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: We have asked the former Head of Civil Service, Mr Peter Ho, to oversee this process and he has agreed to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Government will share the findings and lessons with the public, when the AAR is completed.

sections.label: Peter Ho's information access
sections.summary: Mr Peter Ho has been given access to all information on the Government's response.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Mr Peter Ho has been given access to all information with regard to the Government's response.

sections.label: Wide-ranging lessons from review
sections.summary: The lessons from the after-action review will be wide-ranging, including national resilience, supply chains and national resiliency in broad areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To the second question that Mr Pritam Singh asked, indeed, the lessons that we hope to derive from this AAR will be wide-ranging and will include how we can be more resilient as a nation, how we can improve our supply chains and how we can improve our national resiliency in a broad range of areas.

sections.label: Accountability for monies spent
sections.summary: Mr Leong Mun Wai's question concerns accountability for monies spent, an important but different issue that MOF will take up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The question that Mr Leong Mun Wai has asked, really, is more pertaining to accountability with regard to monies spent, which is an important issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But I think it is a slightly different one and MOF will be happy to take that up.
